title: Measure the stop tolerance with the follower driving c48_long in the surrogate, and fix two follower defects it exposed
summary: A surrogate closed loop lets the waypoint follower read the true pose each control and drive the unchanged c48_long checkpoint over five 1 m routes. With the follower as merged, the body ended 117 to 122 mm from every goal, three of five outside the 0.12 m stop tolerance by up to 2 mm, because the follower retired goals at 0.12 m and the tolerance was the same number; and the command changed 44 to 245 times per route, because the heading gate had no hysteresis and alternated one-tick turns with walks on the policy's 0.014 rad/s heading creep. The follower now retires a goal at 0.06 m, inside the tolerance by the 0.05 m stopping distance, and turns from a 0.05 rad error until it falls inside 0.01 rad. With those two changes the body ends 57 to 66 mm from every goal, the shortest turn is 9 controls and commands change 6 to 33 times per route. No falls on any route. The open-loop drift of up to 298 mm per 20 s walk is corrected in closed loop.
next: Repeat with a simulated Mid-360 odometry pose instead of the true pose, then natively on Spark once the evaluator accepts a command producer.
reason: The navigation example, its CPU tests and one surrogate evidence directory change. Runtime locomotion sources, checkpoints, the approved robot, acceptance gates and roadmap markers remain unchanged.
